environment: macOS arm64; fresh temporary DZMM_NEXT_DATA_DIR; LAN sidecar bound to 0.0.0.0 on an isolated port; no Android device attached

implementation.host_control: The Mac Tauri host exposes an explicit LAN gameplay switch. Switching restarts its sidecar between 127.0.0.1 and 0.0.0.0, sets DZMM_NEXT_LAN_GAMEPLAY, waits for loopback health, and restores the prior listener if the restart fails.
implementation.remote_boundary: With LAN gameplay enabled, a non-loopback source is allowed only under /api/v2/mobile/. It can request and complete pairing, then use bearer-protected gameplay endpoints. World composition, model profiles, host pairing approval/revocation and capabilities are denied before their handlers run.
implementation.local_boundary: Loopback Mac traffic retains authoring and host-control access. LAN gameplay is off by default.

verification.backend: pytest -q: 43 passed; ruff check src tests: passed. The LAN test uses a non-loopback TestClient source to prove protected routes return 403, then completes a real persisted pairing through loopback approval and performs a mobile narrative choice.
verification.desktop_source: npm run build, cargo fmt --check and cargo check: passed.
verification.packaged_build: Fresh PyInstaller sidecar build and CI=true npx tauri build --debug: passed; debug .app and DMG were emitted.
verification.sidecar_smoke: A fresh sidecar actually bound 0.0.0.0. A loopback request reached host capabilities, while a request through the Mac non-loopback interface received 403 for that host route and 200 for a mobile pairing request.

boundary: This is security and packaging evidence for the LAN Host implementation. It does not prove a click through the packaged Tauri WebView, Android QR/manual pairing UX, Android gameplay/recovery, Wi-Fi discovery, disconnect soak, signed artifacts, or physical Mac plus Android LAN acceptance. It does not change the maturity score.
